Ten literal-source-feature items. claim_level_measure.residual_difference_explained: Every one of the 38 passages is exact letter-skeleton contained on its cited page (26 text passages and 12 displays). Each residual difference recorded by the instrument is source-side and of one of three kinds: (a) an insertion of source running head, folio or neighbouring exercise or Comment text between two author sentences, e.g. '12. additional exercises 235 6.80. show that there is a function' on p. 252 and '621 comments on exercises 6.86.' on p. 638; (b) a flattening of sub- and superscripts by extraction, so that e^{-epsilon n} appears inline as e-epsilon n and the fraction of the final display loses its bar; (c) a delimiter-font control byte at a stretched fence or overline, mapped to a space by the instrument and itemised in observed_text_layer_substitutions. None is a reader-side change.

preserved_literal_source_notation: The asked constant: printed with a single raised asterisk at 6.30 pt on physical p. 252 (3 occurrences, 0 double) and on physical p. 638 (1 occurrence, 0 double), and transcribed with a single star in both places. The double-star constant is a different printed symbol set as two raised asterisks at 7.35 pt and occurs only on physical pp. 238 (7 single, 6 double) and 240 (8 single, 6 double); it is transcribed as Phi**_E only there.
The unanchored expansion constant of Exercise 6.23 on physical p. 238 carries no star at all: its Phi is followed directly by the sans-serif E subscript. It is transcribed as Phi_E.

The Comment's denominators: L_e and sum_{e in E(S)} L_e are printed over the edge set E(S), and partial_E S over the vertex set S. The denominator is neither sum_{e in E*(S)} L_e nor |E(S)|, and it differs from the display of the Theorem 6.50 proof on physical p. 240, which uses E*(S). Both are transcribed as printed.
The law and its members are set in angle brackets, <L_i> and <L_e>_{e in E(G)}; these transcribe as ordinary angle brackets and are printed as such.
The nested exponent of the multline*: (1-e^{-epsilon n})^{2^{n}} prints the 2 at 6.3 pt and the n at 5.25 pt, one level above it. The reader preserves both levels.
The final display: numerator 2n+1, denominator cn, and the relation is the two-line approximation symbol, not an equality. Transcribed as printed.

The two phrasings kept apart: the exercise's 'a tail that decays slower than exponentially' and the Comment's 'does not have an exponential tail' are both printed as written and neither is sharpened into the other.

limitations: No pixel inspection of any page was performed by this session; the conclusion rests on text layers and on geometric measurement of span sizes, baselines and fonts only. The five 150 dpi renderings under render/ are stored but were not viewed. Unlike the 6.78 batch, no element of this exercise required a pixel reading.

The PDF text layer of this source has systematic artefacts that a naive substring test misreads: Latin ligatures are decomposed ('innitely', 'satises'), the sans-serif E of the anchored constants is dropped or extracted as an ordinary E, super- and subscripts are flattened, and the stretched delimiters of some formulas are encoded as control bytes of the font txex-bar. In the reader's own text layer seven control characters appear on pages 4 and 5 (five and two), all of them LMMathExtension10 encodings of the big parentheses of the c(1+Phi**_E) display and of the exp(...) in the Comment. All are Type1 delimiter-font encodings surfacing in extraction; none is a missing glyph and none is a rendering defect, and replacement characters are zero everywhere.

Because super- and subscripts are flattened by extraction, exponent and index placement in the reader is not verified by these instruments; it is verified only insofar as LaTeX produced it and latexmk reported no error. The source-side exponent-versus-subscript question is settled from the source page geometry, and the reader-side setting from the TeX source read in full.
